lede: **The Rockmen fight you at home, and they fight you in weather.** Every ship in the hostile pool is Rock, and five of the eight events across the hostile and boarder pools open in an asteroid field or beside a sun — hazards that lock the ship menu for as long as you stay, so no upgrades and no cargo-bay swaps while the rocks are landing. It is a late-run sector by construction — never earlier than five — and you come anyway for the two beacons it must place by name: one opens the **Rock Cruiser quest**, and {{ROCK_CRYSTAL_BEACON}} is the only door in the game to the Crystal worlds — for a ship that already has a Crystal aboard.
callout: **Versus a plain Rock Controlled Sector:** the same pools, the same allocation numbers, the same ships. Four things differ — it can appear once per run, never before sector 5, it adds the two named beacons at the head of the queue, and the **Crystal Lockdown Bomb** drops from rarity 4 to 2, the lowest value that weapon is given in any sector, the Crystal worlds included. The shooting is the same shooting; the reason to come is the top two lines.

section_notes.ROCK_CRYSTAL_BEACON: The way out of the game's normal map, and the **Crystal crew** blue option is the only choice that opens it — the Damaged Stasis Pod on its own will not do. Nothing in this sector can turn one into the other: the pod becomes a Crystal crew member at a Zoltan research facility, and there is none here, so whether this beacon pays was settled a sector or two ago. Without a Crystal aboard the device is a gamble: scrapping it either pays out a large pile of scrap or brings a Rock warship down on you for the vandalism.
section_notes.ROCK_UNLOCK1: No fight here — the Rock warship never turns hostile and jumps away whatever you say. Two of the three replies plant the next marker; ignoring them ends the line on the spot.
section_notes.HOSTILE_ROCK: Rock ships, all five. Three of them arrive with the environment already against you — twice in an asteroid field, once beside a sun.
section_notes.BOARDERS_ROCK: {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SUN}} has no ship fight and no choice at all: two to three Rockmen are aboard the moment you arrive, and the sun is on you the whole time.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_ROCK: Last in the queue and the deepest pool in the sector — ten events sharing whatever the lines above leave behind, which makes everything in here the least dependable thing to plan a route around. That includes the Crystal route's first step: {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} is the **Damaged Stasis Pod**, and picking it up here is already too late to use it, because the device beacon wants the crew member, not the pod. The trap is {{ROCK_STARSHIP_MINE}}, the only event in this pool that can kill a crew member.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_ROCK: Four of the sector's five crew-killing events sit in this one line, and it is filled early enough that the beacons it asks for always land. The question here is never whether the line appears — it is which of twelve very different events you get.
section_notes.QUESTS_ROCK: This line can place nothing at all, and it matters less than it looks: nine events in the sector plant a quest marker, and only five of them are in here — three more sit in the distress line, and the guaranteed {{ROCK_UNLOCK1}} beacon is the ninth. {{ROCK_QUEST_MARRIAGE_START}} is the sector's own: carry the bride to Numa V and hand her over for a random augment, or refuse, keep her as Rock crew, and fight the wedding party.
section_notes.STORE_ROCK: Two, fixed, and third in the queue, so the resupply always happens. In a sector where asteroids keep striking after the enemy is dead and flares burn rooms between fights, what you are really buying at both of them is hull.

steps.title: {{ROCK_UNLOCK1}}
steps.detail: A Rock war vessel sizes up your ship and offers a test. Both defiant answers plant the marker; **Ignore them** ends the chain there and then.

steps.title: Endure the heat
steps.detail: The coordinates put you next to an M-class star with a Rock Assault shooting at you. Killing it pays scrap and stops the chain — what continues it is **surviving until they jump away**.

steps.title: The shipyard
steps.detail: "I am convinced of your strength." The ship unlocks, they patch 29 hull, and they bolt on **Rock Plating** — the same augment that is a blue option at three separate beacons in this sector's pools.

items.text: Level 2 or 3 opens a branch at five separate beacons, the widest gate in the pool — {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}}, {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}}, {{ROCK_ATHIEST}} and {{TRADER_UPGRADES}}.
{{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}}, {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} and {{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}}.
{{ROCK_MANTIS_HUNTER}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} and {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}} all take a Rock crew member's word where yours does not count.
{{ROCK_MANTIS_HUNTER}}, {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} and {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} — the augment the unlock chain pays out at its last step, spent straight back into this sector's pools.
{{ROCK_MANTIS_FREIGHTER}}, {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, and sending it into the flames at {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} instead of a crew member.
One event, and it is the one that matters: {{ROCK_CRYSTAL_BEACON}}.

panels.title: Named things you can leave with

items.text: **Damaged Stasis Pod** at {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} — the only named item the entire pool hands out.
A **random augment** for delivering the bride to Numa V, if you start {{ROCK_QUEST_MARRIAGE_START}} and go through with it.
Rockmen three ways: converted at {{ROCK_ATHIEST}}, bought at {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}}, or kept as **Ariadne** by refusing the wedding.
{{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} is the one beacon that can produce a Mantis, a Rockman or an Engi; {{TAVERN_HIRE}} sells crew outright; **Dr Jones** comes off the burning station at {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}.
28 of the 52 events in the pool can add a crew member — more than half the sector.
**A reactor bar for 10–15 scrap** at {{ROCK_SLUG_ARGUMENT}}: pay off the Rock ship's debt and the Slugs sell you the power.

Five events can kill a crew member outright, and four of them are packed into a distress pool that only gets one or two beacons: {{DISTRESS_INFESTATION}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}} and {{STRANDED_BEACON}}.
Four events put someone aboard. Three are Rockmen — up to three of them at {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SHIP}} and at {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SUN}} — and {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}} sends two to three humans.

Each rock either strips one shield layer or takes 1 hull and the system in that room, they keep coming after the enemy is dead, and they arrive **faster the more shield levels you own**. {{ROCK_FIGHT_ASTEROID}}, {{ROCK_PIRATE_ASTEROID}} and {{ROCK_BOARDERS_ASTEROID}}.

A flare every 28–34 seconds with five seconds of warning: one or two fires while shields hold, three to six when they are down, and every burning room can take hull and system damage with it. {{ROCK_PIRATE_SUN}} and {{ROCK_BOARDERS_SUN}}.

{{ROCK_STARSHIP_MINE}} costs one drone part to cut away, or one missile and 3 hull to detonate. Send someone out to defuse it by hand and **both** wire choices end the same way: the crew member dies, 5 hull, a breach. Engines 5 backs you out of it for nothing.
Demand payment instead of paying at {{ROCK_SLUG_ARGUMENT}} and it opens with 3 hull damage, a system knocked out, and a fight. Freeing a slave at {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} runs 25–45 scrap.

Neither named beacon announces itself. Only stores and distress calls put a marker on the map, so the device and the war vessel are ordinary unexplored dots until you jump in — unless you are carrying **Ruwen**, the Crystal crew member from the stasis pod, who turns {{ROCK_CRYSTAL_BEACON}} into a quest marker you can see from anywhere.

Long-Ranged Scanners splits the distress-marked pool cleanly: only {{ESCORT_BEACON}}, {{FRIENDLY_BEACON}} and {{TRAP_BEACON}} read as a possible ship. A no-ship reading covers everything else, including {{ASTEROID_DERELICT_SHIP}} and every crew-killer that shows a marker at all.

Nine events here plant one, and a marker can only land on a beacon you have not visited that is not a store, not a distress call, not the exit and not already taken by the fleet. Explore half the map first and the candidates thin out — and if this sector came up seventh, a marker with nowhere to go is dropped instead of carried forward.
Not one nebula line in the table, so no clouds convert beacons, sensors work everywhere, and nothing here slows the pursuit: every jump you make advances the fleet at the full rate.
